title: C919 — Inline connector reference
introduction:
This inline connector brings together roof controls, microphone connections, a communication link, power and ground. I treat its drawing like a station map: sharing a concourse does not mean every wire has the same destination.

Start with the face heading and harness identity, find the labeled cavity in that illustration, then read its matching table row. Circuit Number identifies the circuit; Color describes the wire on that particular harness. Function distinguishes supplies, commands, microphone polarity and ground. The LIN bus is a local communication link carrying messages, rather than a simple on/off power connection. Preserve the fuse-or-circuit-breaker alternatives in the supply descriptions.

Use each face independently: wire details can differ across the connector, and conflicting entries need review before combining them into a connection map. Gray shading can be compared with the blank circuit rows, but the drawings have no shading legend or explicit physical viewing-direction statement. Gauge conventions and Size/Used codes are not explained here. This is an identification reference; access, release, probing, electrical test values and repair instructions require separate service information.

edits.why: I check the harness identity before using the drawing. As displayed, the lower-numbered cavity column is on the left, with the other column on the right. The stepped housing outline helps distinguish this illustration from its counterpart; its projections are not labeled as release mechanisms. Gray positions occur at the top and around the middle of this face.

Match the illustration’s cavity label to Cavity, then read across the same row for the circuit identity, wire details, function and terminal entry. Keep microphone polarity, roof-switch direction and latch signal versus VPWR distinct. Similar function labels do not establish that separate cavities are internally connected, and a terminal listing alone does not establish a repair method.

The displayed cavity columns reverse sides relative to the male illustration: the higher-numbered column is on the left. I use the printed labels rather than mentally flipping the other drawing. This outline has prominent projections on the right and a gray position at the top; those visible features help distinguish the drawings without establishing how to handle the physical connector.

Read wire color, gauge and terminal information from this face’s own rows rather than carrying those details over from the male table. Qualifier is where an applicability distinction would belong; an empty cell does not resolve competing assignments. Female cavity 14 lists both roof-up and microphone-positive functions, while female cavity 15 lists both roof-down and microphone-negative functions. These conflicting assignments remain unresolved, so this table cannot support an unqualified combined connection map.

Keep each kit’s service part, engineering shell, material, gauge and cavity-count fields together as its own catalog entry. The two rows list different shells and materials; neither row establishes interchangeability or selects replacement wire. Tin (greased) is the listed material description, not an instruction to apply grease. Pigtail installation requires separate service information.

originalAuthorHold: The female table assigns cavity 14 both CPR24, SWITCH - CONVERTIBLE ROOF UP, and VMEA0, MICROPHONE - AMBIENT NOISE 3 +. Both entries lack qualifiers. The applicable assignment must be resolved; neither entry has been selected or altered.

editorialRevision.scope: Complete independent active-agent review of all 69 primary units, four complete source pages and both figures, and all 5 edits. Original first CLI author covered 61 units and only 4 headings. Complete draft adds pigtail heading and explanation, explicitly identifies both female 14 and 15 assignment conflicts, and covers remaining female rows, pigtail table and raw tail. Original partial author retained separately. Physical assignments remain unresolved for bounded source reading only.
